question: Vijay got an increase of 4% in his sales amount in the first year and 25% in the second year; also with this, his current sales are ₹1,50,800, what was his sales (in ₹) two years ago?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Net percentage increase = a + b + (a × b) ÷ 100

Net increase = 4 + 25 + (4 × 25) ÷ 100 = 29 + 1 = 30%

This means the current sales are 130% of the initial sales.

Initial sales = 1,50,800 × (100 ÷ 130) = 1,16,000

**∴ The correct answer is ₹1,16,000.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Increase in 1st year = 4%

Increase in 2ⁿd year = 25%

Current sales (Final Value) = ₹1,50,800
